$comment: Decision preconditions. Each entry states what a reasonable decision needs, what this session could and could not establish from the repo and from official sources, and the concrete place to look. `answer` stays null until a human or an account confirms it - we do not fill it in.
how_to_read: severity: blocking = no publishable product claim until answered; high = shapes architecture or the first month of editorial; medium = improves accuracy or efficiency. `default_if_unanswered` is what the site does in the meantime, so the build is never blocked by an unknown - only the claim is.

questions.question: Which product is each of the five supplied links actually meant to point at?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Everything product-facing: the Picks table, guide mentions, link placement, the single-link-per-product test.
questions.what_we_have: Five strings of the form https://link.amazon/<9-character token> recorded in the brief on 2026-11-20.
questions.what_we_lack: The product title, brand, marketplace and listing URL behind each token. No official confirmation is reachable from this environment.
questions.how_to_find_out: Open each link in the browser of the machine that owns the Associates account and copy the address bar; or in Associates Central use the link-building tool (GetLink / SiteStripe on the product page) to regenerate a link from the intended listing and compare the /dp/<ASIN> segment. Paste the five final URLs here and the register fills itself.
questions.default_if_unanswered: The five rows publish with blank title, price, rating and listing URL, marked unverified, and no product claim is written anywhere.

questions.question: Are the five tokens truncated ASINs, mistyped ASINs, or an identifier from some other system?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Whether we can auto-correct anything at all, and how the collector should validate incoming links.
questions.what_we_have: A reproducible shape measurement: every token is 9 characters and mixed-case (B04G1MEwY, B02NbDxp3, B00hJ57DV, B0c8moW59, B0f3GKalj).
questions.what_we_lack: An authoritative statement of the ASIN length rule that we were able to open (Seller Central help was not reachable here), and any evidence about how the tokens were captured.
questions.how_to_find_out: Two steps: (1) note where the links came from - a clipboard pass, a spreadsheet, or a link tool; a lost character across all five usually means a copy/paste or export artefact. (2) Confirm the identifier rule from the logged-in Seller Central help or the GetItems reference, then re-run npm run check.
questions.who_can_answer: Account owner + a page we could not reach
questions.default_if_unanswered: The build's shape check reports the length and refuses to treat the token as confirmed; nothing is auto-repaired, because inventing a 10th character would fabricate a product identity.

questions.question: Which Associates account and which marketplace does tracking ID shopnow047c-20 belong to, and is this site's URL registered to it?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Which store links send readers to (amazon.com vs amazon.nl/.de), whether commission accrues at all, and whether the account's site list must be updated.
questions.what_we_have: The ID as written in the brief; it matches the documented tag pattern XXXXX-## (SRC-02 §2(b)) and contains no Amazon mark.
questions.what_we_lack: Whether the ID exists, is active, and lists this domain. Keeping account information accurate is the operator's duty under the Participation Requirements.
questions.how_to_find_out: Associates Central → Account settings → Your sites & channels (confirm the deployed URL is listed) and → Account settings → Tracking IDs (confirm shopnow047c-20 exists). Note the locale switcher: US and non-US accounts have separate documents.
questions.default_if_unanswered: All generated store links carry ?tag=shopnow047c-20 as the operator's stated ID, and the site says the ID is unverified rather than implying an active enrollment.

questions.question: Is the account accepted, provisional, or dormant - and has the early qualifying-sales condition already been met?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Whether the first objective is revenue optimisation or simply staying enrolled; how the calendar is sequenced.
questions.what_we_have: Nothing in the repository speaks to this.
questions.what_we_lack: Account status, the date the application was submitted, and qualifying-sales count to date.
questions.how_to_find_out: Associates Central home and earnings pages show status and reported earnings; the acceptance/decision email shows the application date.
questions.default_if_unanswered: The plan optimises for publishable, compliant pages that can earn their first sales, because that ordering is safe under either account state.

questions.question: Do we have Creators API access yet (which requires at least 10 qualifying sales in the past 30 days)?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Whether automated price/availability/rating ingestion is permitted at all; whether the research agent can have a live data source.
questions.what_we_have: The official prerequisite, quoted: enrolment plus 'at least 10 qualifying sales within the past 30 days to access the PA API through the Creators API' (SRC-05), and confirmation that PA-API 5 returns 403 AccessDeniedException (SRC-06).
questions.what_we_lack: Whether this account clears the threshold, and its credential state.
questions.how_to_find_out: Associates Central → Tools → Creators API: registration status and credential list. If it is unavailable, the page will not let you create a credential.
questions.default_if_unanswered: No price, rating or availability field is populated anywhere on the site, and the automation roadmap starts at 'manual link + manual listing check' until the API gate clears.

questions.question: What commission category and rate apply to the products we would promote?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Any 'revenue per click' arithmetic, niche prioritisation, and whether the ledger should forecast anything at all.
questions.what_we_have: The rate structure lives in the Commission Income Statement Appendix inside the Program Policies (SRC-02), and the payment minimums and check-processing fee sit on the same page - both read from the official text and quoted in the register. We keep the figures out of our own copy so a stale number cannot outlive the source.
questions.what_we_lack: Which category a given listing falls in and the current percentage for it; we extracted no product-specific rate.
questions.how_to_find_out: Associates Central → Help → Program Policies → Appendix, find the row for the store and category; the account's own rate card is the authoritative copy.
questions.who_can_answer: Account owner (or any reader with the same page open)
questions.default_if_unanswered: The campaign ledger stores clicks and orders only; it has no revenue column filled and no forecast anywhere.

questions.question: Which niche does this publication own, and is there measured demand for it?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: The first eight guide titles, the cluster structure, and what 'high-converting products' even means here.
questions.what_we_have: Four editorial hypotheses written in the brief (basket vs oven, capacity checklist, cleanup and counter space, multi-function questions), explicitly labelled as working titles.
questions.what_we_lack: Any query, traffic or competition evidence. No Search Console property, no keyword tool output, no third-party benchmark in the repo.
questions.how_to_find_out: Create the Search Console property for the deployed URL, publish the four hypotheses, then let four to six weeks of impressions and queries pick the fifth topic. Free, first-party, and it replaces instinct.
questions.default_if_unanswered: The four hypotheses are published as methodology guides and no page claims to be about popularity, volume or ranking.

questions.question: Does the site stay on the github.io sub-path or move to a custom domain?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Canonical URLs, sitemap contents, feed links, the disclosure page path, and how easily 'who is the publisher' can be answered.
questions.what_we_have: Pages publishes from branch main at / (SRC-10) to https://sassnarep3-star.github.io/WinC/ (SRC-09: project sites live under /<repo>/).
questions.what_we_lack: The operator's intent, budget, and whether a domain is already owned. Whatever name is chosen cannot contain an Amazon mark (SRC-02 §1(g)).
questions.how_to_find_out: Decide, then: add a CNAME file plus the DNS record, and re-run the generator with the new base_url; canonical, sitemap and feed rewrite themselves.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Everything is generated for the sub-path; base_url is one line in site.config.json.

questions.question: Who is the named human accountable for published claims?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Bylines, the About page, whether the disclosure reads 'I' or 'we', and whether a guide may carry a personal test claim at all.
questions.what_we_have: A desk byline and an explicit provenance note; §5 of the Operating Agreement requires the first-person sentence verbatim, which is a real reason a human identity must exist somewhere.
questions.what_we_lack: A name. We will not invent one: a fabricated reviewer is both a false identity and, under the Endorsement Guides, a misleading endorsement.
questions.how_to_find_out: Operator supplies a name, role and contact route; then set authorship.person_byline and rebuild.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Pages say 'Crisp Report desk', the About page states plainly that a person must review before claims get stronger, and no guide pretends to have tested anything.

questions.question: What first-party performance data exists today?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Whether 'data-driven optimisation' is a plan or a claim; which page gets rewritten first.
questions.what_we_have: Nothing. The repo contained one commit with a 6-byte README when this session started.
questions.what_we_lack: Search Console ownership, analytics history, backlinks, impressions, CTR, and any conversion report.
questions.how_to_find_out: Verify the site in Search Console (a URL-prefix property is fastest), let it collect, and record the first two weeks in data/ledger.csv using only the authorized report.
questions.default_if_unanswered: The ledger ships empty with headers defined, and every 'we will know by' field names its measurement source instead of a guess.

questions.question: Where would event data be collected, on what legal basis, and for how long?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Whether the click counter posts anywhere, what the privacy page must say, and whether an EU-focused site needs a consent step.
questions.what_we_have: GitHub Pages is static - it cannot run a collector. Participation Requirements expect cookie/pixel disclosure (SRC-02 §3(e)); GitHub logs visitor IP addresses (SRC-09). Amazon's own text names the ePrivacy Directive and GDPR as applicable law (SRC-02 §3(a)), which matters because the operator is Netherlands-based.
questions.what_we_lack: A host we control, a retention policy, a processing basis, and a decision on whether aggregate counting is worth the disclosure burden at all.
questions.how_to_find_out: Choose one: (a) keep counting local-only, (b) run the supplied collector on a VPS with 30-day retention, (c) adopt a self-hosted privacy analytics product. Then write the privacy page from the choice, not the other way round.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Collector ships disabled (endpoint: null). Events are counted in the visitor's own browser and never sent; the page says so.

questions.question: Are the 'five defined events' from the brief specified anywhere?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: The measurement schema, and therefore what the ledger columns and the collector accept.
questions.what_we_have: The brief says to record five defined events but does not enumerate them in the text this session received.
questions.what_we_lack: The operator's list, if one exists.
questions.how_to_find_out: Either confirm the five proposed here (page_view, guide_open, outbound_click, product_intent_check, editorial_decision) or supply the original five and we alias them in data/events.json.
questions.default_if_unanswered: We publish a proposed five with explicit field definitions and mark the proposal as ours, not as an existing standard.

questions.question: May we reuse Amazon-supplied images or titles in the layout?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Whether product cards can carry imagery at all, and what the assets folder may contain.
questions.what_we_have: The rule that Program Content may not be altered except proportional resizing and non-meaning-changing truncation, and that it must be removed once it is gone from Amazon (SRC-02 §6(a),(c)). The IP License governs reuse and we could not open it from here.
questions.what_we_lack: The specific image-rights terms and any storage or expiry limits on image URLs.
questions.how_to_find_out: Read the 'Associates Program IP License and Usage Requirements' section of the Program Policies page while logged in, and check the image-serving option in the link tool.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Only our own generated illustrations are used, each labelled as an illustration rather than product imagery.

questions.question: Is there an existing disclosure, privacy policy or cookie notice on the operator's other properties?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Whether this site links to a group policy or must stand alone, and whether wording conflicts need reconciling.
questions.what_we_have: Nothing in the repo references an existing policy.
questions.what_we_lack: Any prior document, the operator's legal entity, and the country of establishment for tax and payment settings (the payment minimums and tax schedules in the Operating Agreement depend on it).
questions.how_to_find_out: Search the operator's other properties; if none exists, keep the standalone pages we ship and update them when a group policy appears.
questions.default_if_unanswered: Standalone disclosure and privacy pages, generated with the same base URL as everything else.

questions.question: What is the pass condition for this project in 90 days?
questions.decision_it_unblocks: Every prioritisation argument in the suggestions board; without it, 'optimise' has no referent.
questions.what_we_have: Two candidate conditions implied by the sources: the enrolment-survival condition (earn qualifying sales early) and a coverage condition (one guide per question the desk can answer without inventing data).
questions.what_we_lack: The operator's threshold - indexed pages, impressions, clicks, click-through-to-listing rate, orders, or a revenue number.
questions.how_to_find_out: Pick one primary and one guard-rail metric, write them into data/ledger.csv as targets, and the weekly note reports against them.
questions.default_if_unanswered: The site reports coverage and verification state (pages live, rows unresolved, gate failures) and stays silent on success.
